raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The CI monitor, which runs every 12 hours, can mark a file as a possible timeout when pytest listed other files as failed. A maintainer who reads its step summary or JSON artifact then looks at the wrong test. In monitor [run 41441787333](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41441787333) on 2026-11-02, all 10 inferred timeouts show this, in `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd` partitions, on files with no failure row.

With this PR, those 10 jobs name the files that pytest listed, 14 jobs that named no file now name one, and 94 with logs still name none. In a saved-data replay on 5 AMD runs, step summary rows with a timeout mark go from 32 to 0.

In [job 124857721211](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41309823139/job/124857721211), the monitor blames `test_component_residency.py` (`PASSED` lines, no failure row), and the real failure is `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py`.

With no custom `Test Summary`, the parser skips pytest's failure rows and names the file that last printed `server_args:`, even a file that passed.

I found no other open PR that changes this parser.

## Modifications

The parser now reads pytest's `FAILED`, `ERROR`, and `SUBFAILED` rows before it infers a timeout.

- The runner's `retry failed items` marker discards the attempt it replaces. A new session keeps earlier failures.
- A `-q` result after a session header is a nested run, so its rows do not count.
- Inference reads only lines after the last session header or pytest result and adds to known failures.
- `ci_auto_bisect.py` calls this parser, replacing its older copy with the same problem.

Rows that start with `Limit` show deliberate limits.

## Accuracy Tests

`a8f2b32f8d` and `255251d2c7` are commits from before I squashed this branch onto main `7b88f09239`. The squash kept the same diff, and I did not repeat these runs on it. On the squashed commit, only pre-commit and `test_ci_failures_analysis.py` ran, on CPU, and the test file found no failure.

| Input | Merge base | Head (a8f2b32f8d or 255251d2c7, same parser file) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parse_test_summary` replay on real logs: monitor run 41441787333, 140 jobs (130 with no summary and the 10 inferred, 22 of the 130 have no log and give `None` on both sides), 24 results changed | 10 inferred results with no failure row, 14 `None` | Those 10 become files that pytest listed, those 14 become named files |
| Same replay, 469 unique logs, 37 results changed: that run, a sample of 331 jobs that failed (84 job families, at most 5 logs per family, 10 changed, not a rate), and 62 cached logs (6 changed) | 12 inferred, 25 `None` | 37 listed, 0 inferred to `None`. No custom-summary log changed, and each file that head named in a changed result has a pytest row in its log |
| Monitor `main()` replay on saved GitHub responses and real logs, `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd` jobs of 5 AMD runs | 32 step summary rows with a timeout mark (9 file and job pairs) | 0 such rows, and the rows name files that pytest listed |
| [Job 121938136106](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40427865857/job/121938136106) | `test_text_encoder_loader.py` (inferred) | `test_nomas.py` |
| Job 124757091005 | `test_wan_animate_2_config.py` (inferred) | `test_http_auth.py`, `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py` |
| Job 124757090997 | `None` | `test_disagg_server.py` |
| Job 105808074660 and four more AMD jobs | `None` | `test_eagle_utils.py` |
| Lab, pytest 9.2.0, subTest-only failure | `None` | `test_subtest_only.py` |
| Lab, confirmed failure, then a hang and SIGKILL | `test_unittest_hangs.py` (inferred) | `test_pytest_fails.py`, `test_unittest_hangs.py` (inferred) |
| Job 124757091005, sampled cuts in lines 7700 to 8425 | `test_component_residency.py` (inferred) | `None` |
| Job 124757091005, cuts in lines 7691 to 7693 and 7731 to 7733 (about 16 ms each) | `test_component_residency.py` (inferred) | generated `test_retry.py` |
| Lab, `server_args:` in a passing session, then a silent hang and SIGKILL | `test_args_passes.py` (inferred) | `None` |
| Repository tests on one B200 (scratch-installed imports), SIGKILL just after a nested `-q` result | Not recorded | `None` |
| Limit, real server on one B200: inference needs `server_args:` or `server_args =`, and SRT logs `server_args=`, so a hang with no earlier failure stays unattributed | `None` | `None` |
| Limit, lab: a `run_suite` step dies before `Test Summary`, so a recovered retry stays listed | `None` | `test_retry_recovers.py` |
| Limit, lab: any `-q` result after a framed session clears that session's failures (framed failure, then passing `-q`) | `None` | `None` |
| Limit, lab: a failing `-q` file is not listed (failing `-q` file after a framed session, then a hang and SIGKILL) | `test_unittest_hangs.py` (inferred) | `test_unittest_hangs.py` (inferred) |
| Limit, job 122358685306: logs before #46916 print the marker after the retry | `test_wan_animate_2_config.py` (inferred) | generated `test_retry.py` paths, `test_cosmos3_multiview.py`, `test_host_sync.py` |
| Pre-commit and the test file (B200 lab CPU) | Test file: the new cases fail except the hang, nested, and passing-session guards | No failures at 255251d2c7 and on a trial merge with upstream/main 035670b685 |
| Auto bisect replay of `analyze_scheduled_failures` (only its fetch functions faked), 294 logs of failed jobs from scheduled `pr-test.yml` runs, 2026-08-05 to 2026-11-02 | 7 results differ from head. All 7 are older than #37436, which moved the diffusion jobs to `test/run_suite.py` on 2026-09-07, so those jobs now print `Test Summary` | The next four rows are the only changes |
| Auto bisect, job 92294591883 (bisect run 31026268061) | `test_server_args.py` (inferred) | `test_glm_image_ar.py`, `test_glm_image_multi_output.py` |
| Auto bisect, job 94751935627 (bisect run 31815647304) | `test_server_args.py` (inferred) | `test_minimax_h3_admission.py` |
| Auto bisect, job 100224824164 (bisect run 33648651201) | `test_server_args.py` (inferred) | `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py` |
| Auto bisect, jobs 93281526981, 93664878572, 96256309811, 100224886055 | `<job-level>` | `test_server_1_gpu.py` |
| Auto bisect, second replay of 82 logs that the 294 miss: 71 `pr-test-extra-finish` jobs, which the bisect does not exclude, and 11 jobs from 6 runs (2026-10-15 to 2026-10-23) whose job list returns HTTP 502 at `per_page=100` | Same as head | No result changes |
| Auto bisect, jobs 105970463638 and 105983459255, the only failures in direct pytest steps in this window, killed with no failure row | `<job-level>` | `<job-level>` |
| Auto bisect, lab, pytest 9.2.0: a real failure in a `set -e` chain of `pytest -q` or in a `pytest -v` step, the direct step shapes in `pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml` and the simulator workflows. Lab only, because no CI log in the replay window has a direct pytest step that lists a failure | `<job-level>` | The failing file |
| Auto bisect, 45 listed jobs with no usable log: 42 dated 2026-07-28 to 2026-08-04 return HTTP 410, and 3 `base-c-test-8-gpu-h20` jobs return HTTP 404 | Not replayed | Not replayed |

For the auto bisect, no replayed log since 2026-09-08 changes the result, so today's benefit is the direct pytest steps and one parser instead of two.

Not verified: a live monitor run, a full auto bisect run with its LLM call, the monitor's exact log bytes (the replay fetched logs later), CI workflows behind the draft gate, and jobs in 18 cancelled runs. No real step timeout reached inference, so only synthetic and unit cases cover hangs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed benchmark was run. Serving does not change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""Regressions for attributing CI failures from completed pytest attempts."""
+
+import importlib.util
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=15, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+_SCRIPT = (
+    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "scripts/ci_monitor/ci_failures_analysis.py"
+)
+_SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("ci_failures_analysis", _SCRIPT)
+_MODULE = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_SPEC)
+_SPEC.loader.exec_module(_MODULE)
+
+_SESSION = "================ test session starts ================\n"
+_SERVER_ARGS = "server_args: model_path='test-model'\n"
+
+
+def _failed_session(path):
+    return (
+        _SESSION + "================ short test summary info ================\n"
+        f"FAILED {path}::test_case\n"
+        "================ 1 failed in 1.00s ================\n"
+    )
+
+
+_PASSED_SESSION = _SESSION + "================ 1 passed in 1.00s ================\n"
+_RETRY_MARKER = (
+    "Starting pytest attempt 2/7: retry failed items for 1 assigned item(s)\n"
+)
+_TAIL = """================ Pytest Tail Summary ================
+Attempt 1 failure summary:
+  FAILED test/test_old.py::test_old
+====================================================
+"""
+
+
+class TestCIFailuresAnalysis(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        self.analyzer = _MODULE.SGLangFailuresAnalyzer("")
+        self.addCleanup(self.analyzer.session.close)
+
+    def _failed_paths(self, logs):
+        summary = self.analyzer.parse_test_summary(logs)
+        return (
+            [test["full_path"] for test in summary["failed_tests"]] if summary else []
+        )
+
+    def test_pytest_failures_override_last_running_test(self):
+        """A passing loader must not replace the failures listed by pytest."""
+        summary = self.analyzer.parse_test_summary(
+            """
+sglang/test/test_text_encoder_loader.py::TestLoader::test_quantized [10-27 01:41:06]
+server_args: model_path='test-model'
+PASSED
+sglang/test/test_text_encoder_loader.py::TestLoader::test_restore PASSED
+================ short test summary info ================
+FAILED sglang/test/test_nomas.py::test_fused_qk_norm
+FAILED sglang/test/test_nomas.py::test_fused_swiglu
+FAILED sglang/test/test_nomas.py::test_growing_history
+=== 3 failed, 1558 passed, 16 skipped, 64 warnings, 107 subtests passed in 154.07s ===
+"""
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            summary,
+            {
+                "passed": 0,
+                "total": 0,
+                "failed_tests": [
+                    {
+                        "test_file": "test_nomas.py",
+                        "full_path": "sglang/test/test_nomas.py",
+                    }
+                ],
+            },
+        )
+
+    def test_timestamped_ansi_errors_and_parametrized_failures(self):
+        lines = [
+            "================ short test summary info ================",
+            "FAILED test/a/test_values.py::TestValues::test_shape[32 - 64] - AssertionError",
+            "FAILED test/a/test_values.py::TestValues::test_shape[128] - AssertionError",
+            "ERROR test/b/test_values.py::TestValues::test_setup[False] - RuntimeError",
+            "ERROR test/test_collection.py - ImportError",
+            "SUBFAILED(dtype=torch.float32) test/test_sub.py::TestSub::test_sub - Error",
+            "================ 3 failed, 2 errors in 1.00s ================",
+        ]
+        for prefix in (
+            "2026-10-27T01:41:23.8215231Z ",
+            "test-job\tUNKNOWN STEP\t2026-10-27T01:41:23.8215231Z ",
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(prefix=prefix):
+                logs = "\n".join(f"{prefix}\x1b[31m{line}\x1b[0m" for line in lines)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    self._failed_paths(logs),
+                    [
+                        "test/a/test_values.py",
+                        "test/b/test_values.py",
+                        "test/test_collection.py",
+                        "test/test_sub.py",
+                    ],
+                )
+
+    def test_retry_replaces_previous_attempt(self):
+        initial = _failed_session("test/test_old.py")
+        for logs, expected in (
+            (initial + _RETRY_MARKER + _PASSED_SESSION + _TAIL, []),
+            (
+                initial + _RETRY_MARKER + _failed_session("test/test_new.py") + _TAIL,
+                ["test/test_new.py"],
+            ),
+            (initial + _TAIL + _RETRY_MARKER + _PASSED_SESSION, ["test/test_old.py"]),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(logs=logs):
+                self.assertEqual(self._failed_paths(logs), expected)
+
+    def test_real_runner_retry_and_plain_sequential_sessions(self):
+        """Parse real output, so a changed retry marker or pytest format fails here."""
+        program = (
+            "import subprocess, sys\n"
+            "from sglang.multimodal_gen.test.runner.pytest_runner import run_pytest\n"
+            "run_pytest(['test_recovers.py'])\n"
+            "sys.stdout.flush()\n"
+            "for name in ('test_fails.py', 'test_passes.py'):\n"
+            "    subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', name])\n"
+        )
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
+            (Path(root) / "test_recovers.py").write_text(
+                "from pathlib import Path\n"
+                "def test_slow():\n"
+                "    marker = Path(__file__).with_suffix('.attempt')\n"
+                "    if not marker.exists():\n"
+                "        marker.touch()\n"
+                "        assert False, '[performance] Validation failed'\n"
+            )
+            (Path(root) / "test_fails.py").write_text(
+                "def test_x():\n    assert False\n"
+            )
+            (Path(root) / "test_passes.py").write_text("def test_x():\n    pass\n")
+            result = subprocess.run(
+                [sys.executable, "-c", program],
+                cwd=root,
+                env={**os.environ, "PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD": "1"},
+                capture_output=True,
+                text=True,
+                timeout=120,
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(self._failed_paths(result.stdout), ["test_fails.py"])
+
+    def test_unfinished_session_keeps_earlier_failures(self):
+        summary = self.analyzer.parse_test_summary(
+            _failed_session("test/test_old.py")
+            + _SESSION
+            + "test/test_current.py::test_current\n"
+            + _SERVER_ARGS
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(summary["incomplete"])
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [test["full_path"] for test in summary["failed_tests"]],
+            ["test/test_old.py", "test/test_current.py"],
+        )
+
+    def test_passing_session_has_no_summary(self):
+        """An empty summary would hide the monitor's missing-summary diagnostic."""
+        self.assertIsNone(self.analyzer.parse_test_summary(_PASSED_SESSION))
+
+    def test_hang_after_finished_session_is_inferred(self):
+        """A unittest file prints no session header, so a pytest result can precede it."""
+        summary = self.analyzer.parse_test_summary(
+            _PASSED_SESSION
+            + "Begin (1/2):\npython3 /repo/test_hang.py\n"
+            + _SERVER_ARGS
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(summary["incomplete"])
+        self.assertEqual(summary["failed_tests"][0]["test_file"], "test_hang.py")
+
+    def test_nested_quiet_run_is_not_a_failure(self):
+        """test_sequential_server_requests.py runs `pytest -q` inside its session."""
+        summary = self.analyzer.parse_test_summary(
+            _SESSION
+            + "test/test_outer.py::test_nested\n"
+            + "================ short test summary info ================\n"
+            + "FAILED test_generated.py::test_generated[failed]\n"
+            + "2 failed, 2 passed, 4 warnings in 22.69s\n"
+            + "PASSED\n"
+            + "test/test_outer.py::test_after_nested\n"
+            + _SERVER_ARGS
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(summary["incomplete"])
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [test["full_path"] for test in summary["failed_tests"]],
+            ["test/test_outer.py"],
+        )
+
+    def test_quiet_run_outside_a_session_is_a_failure(self):
+        """Simulator jobs run `pytest -q`, which prints no session header."""
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._failed_paths(
+                "================ short test summary info ================\n"
+                "FAILED test/test_quiet.py::test_case - AssertionError\n"
+                "1 failed, 1 passed in 1.00s\n"
+            ),
+            ["test/test_quiet.py"],
+        )
+
+    def test_auto_bisect_targets_the_failures_pytest_listed(self):
+        """The bisect must not spend its analysis on a passing loader."""
+        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+            "ci_auto_bisect", _SCRIPT.with_name("ci_auto_bisect.py")
+        )
+        bisect = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+        with mock.patch.dict(sys.modules, {"ci_failures_analysis": _MODULE}):
+            spec.loader.exec_module(bisect)
+        logs = (
+            _SESSION
+            + "test/test_loader.py::test_quantized\n"
+            + _SERVER_ARGS
+            + "PASSED\n"
+            + "================ short test summary info ================\n"
+            + "FAILED test/test_nomas.py::test_case\n"
+            + "================ 1 failed, 1 passed in 1.00s ================\n"
+        )
+        with mock.patch.multiple(
+            bisect,
+            fetch_nvidia_scheduled_runs=lambda token: [{"id": 1}],
+            fetch_jobs_for_run=lambda run_id, token: [
+                {"name": "unit", "conclusion": "failure", "id": 2}
+            ],
+            fetch_job_logs=lambda job_id, token: logs,
+        ):
+            targets, _ = bisect.analyze_scheduled_failures("")
+        self.assertEqual([target.test_file for target in targets], ["test_nomas.py"])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
